_comment: Narration for the Duum demo (out/duum/cut.mp4). Each cue names the BEAT it lands on, from that scene's .beats.jsonl, so the voice tracks the picture. Budgeted at Brian's MEASURED 2.9 words/sec (from the UnoDOS OS demo). Claims checked against source: DUUM.PY is Python on PYRT/MicroPython; uno.read_at streams the WAD lump-by-lump (never slurped); render() (BSP walk + column loop) is Python, cv.wall_span/mask_span/flat_span are C; monster AI + weapons + E1M1-E1M9 exist. Combat footage shows firing + health dropping, NOT a clean framed kill, so the combat cue only claims what is on screen (they shoot back, health drops, you fire).
_voice: Brian - Deep, Resonant and Comforting (matches arin's UnoDOS OS demo)

cues.text: This is Doom, running inside UnoDOS - and written entirely in Python.
It runs as an ordinary app, on the operating system's own Python runtime.
It streams a real Doom game file a piece at a time, never loading the whole thing into memory.
The walls, the floor, the ceiling and the sky are all drawn from that file, as a first-person, perspective-correct view.
The former humans shoot back, and your health drops as you push through, firing.
Weapons, monsters and pickups, across all nine levels of the first episode.
Only the per-pixel drawing is C. The geometry and the game logic are Python.
Every other port of this system rebuilds its own apps in each machine's language.
Duum does the reverse - a whole outside game engine, in nothing but Python.
